title: Data Analysis of LIS Data Center Users
short: Time series analysis and backend architecture for HPC usage data — reliable database interaction is foundational to any data center's operations.
body:
The foundation of any data analysis project is a stable, fault-tolerant database that adheres to the principles of the CAP theorem. There are several approaches to connecting to such a data source and initiating analysis, one of the most effective being Object-Relational Mapping (ORM). In this project, we used a MySQL server together with Python and R, applying time series techniques such as ARMA to analyze usage data by the Luxembourg Income Study (LIS) data center users.

Method

The project was structured in two phases. The first phase involved integrating multiple existing databases and tables into a single, consolidated table to serve as the foundation for analysis. ORMs were used throughout this process to establish connections, execute queries, and transform and retrieve data efficiently. The second phase focused on analysis and visualization: we used the Shiny library in R to build an interactive dashboard, enabling system administrators to monitor and evaluate usage of the data center's HPC clusters. Since usage data is generated daily across all HPC users, maintaining up-to-date statistics is essential for the LIS data center to effectively manage the resources it provides to its users.

Results

The project delivered an interactive dashboard alongside a continuously growing consolidated table, built by integrating data from multiple source databases into a single analytical foundation.
